Executive summary

One customer. Different needs. Different conversations. One learning journey that prepares you for all of them.

The Conversation is a customer-centric learning experience designed to transform how MAGRABi store teams engage with customers — moving beyond scripted selling towards confident, needs-led consultative conversations.

Through AI-generated realistic videos featuring lifelike characters inspired by the MAGRABi retail environment, learners engage with four recurring customer segments — including the hesitant, the Budget-conscious customer, and the customer who relies on a companion's input. Their evolving needs challenge learners to adapt their approach across increasingly demanding situations.

A recurring Instructor accompanies learners throughout the journey, analyzing critical moments, highlighting key behaviours, and guiding them towards more effective customer interactions.

Across six progressive modules, learners build three core capabilities: Diagnose the Pain, Differentiate the Claims, and Demonstrate the Gain. Each is developed individually before being integrated into The Full Conversation, followed by practical application in the store environment. Through consequence-based branching, guided reflection, and progressive practice, learners move from guided understanding to confident, independent performance.

The result: a realistic, immersive learning experience that turns customer understanding into relevant recommendations, stronger conversations, and meaningful customer experiences.

Our understanding

The most important customer conversation happens in the five minutes between the exam room and the price. Yet, it has never been taught as one consistent method.

In MAGRABi's retail environment, the challenge is not simply knowing the product. It is knowing how to turn clinical insight and product expertise into a customer conversation that feels relevant, personal, and convincing.

The Nature of the Challenge

The Five-Minute Window

  1. Exam Room
  2. Observe & Read Cues
  3. Ask & Clarify
  4. Uncover the Real Need
  5. Connect the Right Solution
  6. Demonstrate the Gain
  7. Price
5 Minutes

The brief identifies a clear gap: approximately 80% behavioural and 20% technical knowledge. Store teams need more than product information or sales scripts. They need a shared method for understanding what matters to each customer, uncovering the real need behind the initial request, and connecting the right recommendation to a benefit the customer can recognize and experience.

This means moving beyond opening with frames or listing lens features, towards reading customer cues, asking purposeful questions, reflecting the customer's needs, and demonstrating value before discussing price.

From Product Knowledge to Customer-Centred Conversations

Our understanding is that the solution must establish one consistent selling method across the retail team — not a collection of disconnected product lessons.

The learning experience therefore builds the capabilities progressively: Diagnose the Pain, Differentiate the Claims, and Demonstrate the Gain, bringing them together in a complete customer conversation. Learners must be able to recognize different needs, make relevant recommendations, demonstrate value before price, and guide the conversation towards a meaningful decision.

One Complete Customer Conversation

Success must extend beyond course completion. The programme is designed to support measurable improvements in Exam-to-Frame Conversion, Multi-Pair Conversion, and Average Basket Value, while building the behaviours that make those outcomes possible.

The design principle is clear: build one conversation, not a set of modules — and make the right behaviour easier to apply in every store, every day.

The Learning Design

The 6-Week Learning Journey

One connected journey. Three progressive phases. One complete customer conversation.

The Conversation is designed as a six-week blended learning experience that progressively develops the skills, confidence, and behaviours store teams need to deliver one complete, customer-centred conversation.

One shared behavioural focus each week aligns advisors and managers around the same capability. Advisors develop it through interactive learning and realistic customer scenarios, while managers reinforce it through coaching and observation. Daily 10-minute huddles turn the same focus into repeated practice, increasing in complexity through different customer profiles, needs, and situations.

The progression follows three core skills: Diagnose the Pain, Differentiate the Claims, and Demonstrate the Gain through relevant Proof. Each builds on the previous one, preparing learners to bring all three together in The Full Conversation.

One weekly focus. Aligned learning. Continuous practice. Consistent performance on the floor.

What Powers the Learning Experience

Five interconnected elements bring the learning experience to life:

1 AI-Generated Realistic Customer Videos

Realistic customer interactions set within a MAGRABi-inspired retail environment. These videos create authentic situations in which learners can observe customer behaviour, interpret reactions, make decisions, and experience the consequences of different approaches.

2 A Recurring Instructor

A consistent Instructor guides learners throughout the journey, interpreting customer cues and highlighting effective behaviours. Within interactive branching scenarios, the Instructor delivers voice-led feedback in response to learners’ choices, explaining the impact of their decisions and reinforcing more effective behaviours.

3 Four Recurring Customer Profiles

Four customer profiles return across M2, M3, M4, and M5. Their needs and situations become progressively more demanding as additional steps of the conversation are introduced. This continuity allows learners to experience how the same customer type can require a more developed response as their capabilities grow.

4 Consequence-Based Branching Scenarios

Learning moves beyond selecting correct answers. Learners make decisions within realistic customer conversations and see how each choice influences the customer's response. The visible consequences create opportunities to reflect, adjust, and practise more effective behaviours.

5 Practice, Coaching & Floor Certification

Structured digital practice is reinforced through facilitated activities, peer roleplay, manager coaching, and observed in-store performance. The objective is not simply to complete learning activities, but to transfer the method into everyday customer interactions.

Phase 01 — FOUNDATION · Weeks 0–1 | Establishing the Mindset

M0 — Kick-off & Manager Alignment

Align managers on The Conversation methodology, programme expectations, performance KPIs, and their role in reinforcing the expected behaviours on the shop floor.

Learning Components

  • Manager Kick-off Workshop: Aligns managers on programme objectives, KPIs, coaching responsibilities, and assessment gates.

Phase Outcome: Managers are equipped to coach and reinforce the methodology throughout the journey.

Phase 01 — FOUNDATION · Weeks 0–1 | Establishing the Mindset

M1 — The Retail Primal Brain

Explore the drivers of customer decisions and how the retail environment, advisor approach, and sensory stimuli shape the customer experience.

Learning Components

  • Intro Video: Three Hero Film versions (approximately 90 seconds each), followed by an Instructor-led Video debriefing the three approaches and introducing the learning journey and course outline.
  • Interactive Six Stimuli: A separate interactive retail environment where learners explore how each stimulus shapes the customer experience.

Phase Outcome: Learners explain key factors influencing customer decisions and the principles of customer-centred selling.

Phase 02 — BUILD · Weeks 2–4 | Developing the Three Core Skills

M2 — Diagnose the Pain

Develop purposeful questioning and active listening to uncover the functional, emotional, and trust-related needs behind the customer’s initial request.

Learning Components

  • Instructor-led Micro-module: Introduces the Pain discovery approach and purposeful questioning.
  • Interactive Video-led Branching Scenarios: Four customer situations where learners practise questioning and uncover underlying needs. Each decision triggers a branching video sequence showing the customer’s reaction and the consequences of the choice, followed by contextual Instructor voice feedback. Scenario performance is scored, and learners can revisit alternative choices to explore different outcomes.
  • Completion Requirement: Complete any 2 of the 4 scenarios. The remaining scenarios are optional for additional practice.

Phase Outcome: Learners identify underlying customer needs through purposeful questioning and active listening.

Phase 02 — BUILD · Weeks 2–4 | Developing the Three Core Skills

M3 — Differentiate the Claims

Connect identified customer needs to relevant MAGRABi Claims, communicating meaningful product differences rather than simply listing features.

Learning Components

  • Instructor-led Micro-module: Introduces Claim selection and differentiation, with a brief recap of Pain.
  • Interactive Video-led Branching Scenarios: Four customer situations where learners select and communicate relevant Claims, with branching video reactions and contextual Instructor feedback.
  • Completion Requirement: Complete any 2 of the 4 scenarios.

Phase Outcome: Learners match relevant Claims to customer needs and communicate meaningful product differentiation.

Phase 02 — BUILD · Weeks 2–4 | Developing the Three Core Skills

M4 — Demonstrate the Gain

Turn product Claims into tangible customer benefits through relevant Proof and demonstrations, helping customers experience the value before price enters the conversation.

Learning Components

  • Instructor-led Micro-module: Introduces Proof and Gain demonstration, with brief recaps of Pain and Claims.
  • Interactive Video-led Branching Scenarios: Four customer situations where learners make decisions, with branching video sequences and contextual Instructor feedback.
  • Completion Requirement: Complete any 2 of the 4 scenarios.

Phase Outcome: Learners demonstrate tangible customer value through relevant Proof.

Integrated Practice & Performance Experience | Following Module 4

Customer-in-the-Seat Workshop

Learning Components

  • Integrated Skill Practice: Brings the three core skills — Diagnose the Pain, Differentiate the Claims, and Demonstrate the Gain — into one facilitated practice experience.
  • Persona-Based Team Challenge: Advisors rotate through customer, advisor, and facilitator roles, applying the methodology in realistic customer situations.
  • Recorded Practice & Feedback: Roleplays are recorded to support structured observation, peer feedback, and manager-led debriefs.

Experience Outcome: Advisors integrate all three skills in realistic customer conversations, building confidence and readiness for independent in-store application.

The proposed workshop structure and facilitation approach are outlined in further detail below.

Phase 03 — PERFORM · Weeks 5–6 | Integrating the Skills into One Conversation

M5 — The Full Conversation

Bring Pain, Claims, and Gain together in one complete customer conversation, from discovery and recommendation to demonstration, objection handling, and guiding the customer towards a decision.

Learning Components

  • Instructor-led Revision Video: Briefly revisits the three core capabilities before the scenarios.
  • End-to-end Customer Conversation Scenarios: Four continuous video-led scenarios featuring independent decisions, with an overall score and Instructor feedback after each scenario.
  • Completion Requirement: Complete any 2 of the 4 scenarios.

Phase Outcome: Learners independently deliver a complete customer conversation integrating all three core skills.

Phase 03 — PERFORM · Weeks 5–6 | Integrating the Skills into One Conversation

M6 — In-Store Application & Certification

Demonstrate the complete methodology in a real customer interaction, assessed by the branch manager against MAGRABi’s ten-item floor checklist.

Learning Components

  • Live In-Store Assessment: One observed customer conversation, followed by assessment review and manager sign-off.

Phase Outcome: Learners demonstrate independent, customer-centred performance on the shop floor.

Ongoing Coaching & Reinforcement

Weekly Manager Coaching

Managers use individual and team performance insights to identify strengths, address skill gaps, and set focused coaching priorities. Each weekly session centres on the priority skill, helping advisors translate learning into more effective customer interactions and consistently reinforce the target behaviours.

Daily Skill Huddles

Short, 10-minute team huddles reinforce the weekly skill focus through practical prompts, quick discussions, and relevant customer situations. They keep the target behaviours visible and encourage consistent application during daily store interactions.

Customer-in-the-Seat Workshop
An Integrated Practice & Performance Framework

We propose bringing three existing facilitated activities together under one overarching Customer-in-the-Seat Workshop framework:

  • M2 — Pain Discovery Workshop
  • M4 — In-Store Demo Lab
  • M5 — Full Conversation Workshop

Rather than treating these as disconnected activities, this approach creates a structured progression from focused skill application to practical demonstration and, ultimately, a complete customer conversation integrating all three core skills.

Why This Approach?

Stronger Learning Integration: A shared practice framework enables advisors to progressively apply individual skills in increasingly realistic customer interactions, moving beyond isolated exercises towards confident, integrated performance on the sales floor.

Streamlined Operational Delivery: For MAGRABi, a common facilitation framework, shared practice tools, and consistent behavioural observation criteria create a more manageable delivery model, reducing duplication in preparation while preserving each activity’s specific objectives, format, duration, and learning environment.

How the Experience Works
1
Facilitated Skill Practice

Each existing activity retains its specific learning objective while following a shared practice approach. Participants apply the target skill through guided exercises, practical demonstrations, and facilitator-led activities appropriate to each module.

2
Persona-Based Team Challenge

Participants receive Role Cards assigning them a defined role and customer persona, including customer context, underlying needs, behaviours, and potential objections.

Participants rotate through three roles:

Challenges introduce realistic customer situations, unexpected responses, and increasing levels of complexity, testing skill application rather than recall.

3
Performance Feedback & Coaching

Practice is supported by structured observation, peer feedback, and manager guidance. Feedback focuses on demonstrated behaviours, recognizing effective approaches and identifying specific development priorities.

These observations complement LMS learner reporting, giving managers a broader view of scenario performance and practical skill application to inform subsequent coaching priorities.

Technical Solution & LMS Integration

The proposed learning experience is designed for delivery through MAGRABi’s Absorb LMS, using SCORM 1.2, subject to technical validation of the platform’s capabilities.

LMS Integration

All digital modules and scenario-based assessments will be developed for integration with MAGRABi’s Absorb LMS, subject to technical validation.

SCORM Tracking & Scoring

Digital content will be developed for SCORM 1.2 compatibility, with learner progress, completion, and assessment scores tracked through Absorb, subject to its supported capabilities.

Performance will be assessed across the three core factors: Pain, Claim, and Gain.

Randomization & Retry Logic

Scenario randomization, question pooling, and retry logic will be designed to meet the agreed M2–M5 assessment requirements. The final implementation will depend on technical validation of Absorb’s capabilities and any additional solution required.

Learning Reports & Progress Dashboard

Absorb’s native reporting will be evaluated for learner and store-level insights, including factor-level scores. An external reporting solution may be considered if required.

Technical Validation

The final solution will be confirmed following validation of SCORM compatibility, assessment logic, reporting, mobile access, and maintenance requirements.

Language & Localization

Arabic is the primary language of production. All scripts are originally developed in Arabic by Saudi writers, using natural Saudi dialect for customer and advisor dialogue and clear, simple Modern Standard Arabic for on-screen instructions and explanations.

English is retained for the optometrist clinical track and established product terminology, where required. Arabic content is accompanied by English subtitles, delivered in editable SRT or VTT formats.

All screens, templates, and print materials are designed right-to-left first, with English layouts derived from the Arabic designs.

Aligning Delivery with the Ramadan Calendar

The Consideration

Changes in store operating hours, customer footfall, and staff availability during Ramadan and Eid may affect programme participation and implementation.

Our Recommendation

Protect the pilot delivery milestone while allowing flexibility in the learning rollout:

  • Before Ramadan: Deliver pilot assets and complete the Foundation phase (M0 and M1).
  • After Eid al-Fitr: Launch the Build and Perform phases (M2–M6), including the Customer-in-the-Seat Workshop.

This sequencing helps protect learning continuity while taking branch operating conditions into account. The final rollout schedule remains subject to MAGRABi’s decision.
